instantiated_cells.justification: State agencies that file a statement under § 13.695 (covering officers/employees paid a salary whose duties include influencing legislative action) are not subject to the licensing/registration provisions, so executive branch agencies are not required to register as lobbyists.

An elective state official (which includes the governor) is not subject to the licensing/registration/reporting provisions when acting in an official capacity, so the governor’s office is not required to register as a lobbyist.
Independent state agencies fall within the definition of 'agency' and, if filing under § 13.695, are exempted from lobbyist licensing and principal registration requirements under § 13.621(2).

The subchapter does not apply to 'lobbying of an agency official by an agency official of a different agency or another agency official of the same agency,' so government agencies lobbying other agencies are not required to register as lobbyists for that conduct.

A 'member or employee of the legislature' (legislative branch officials/employees) is not subject to the lobbying regulatory provisions when acting in an official capacity, so they are not required to register as lobbyists.

An individual paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying is a 'lobbyist' and, unless exempt, may not lobby as a lobbyist unless licensed and authorized, which applies to lobbyists working for lobbying firms.

Any 'person' (which can include local governmental units) that employs a lobbyist is a 'principal' and must register if it exceeds $500 in nonexempt lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year.

Except as authorized under § 13.621, no person may engage in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under § 13.63 and authorized under § 13.65, meaning lobbyists must obtain a license (i.e., register) to lobby.
Every principal that exceeds $500 in nonexempt lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year must file a registration statement with the commission within 10 days after exceeding $500.

The registration requirement applies to 'every principal' and a principal is 'any person who employs a lobbyist,' which encompasses public entities other than state agencies when they employ lobbyists and exceed the $500 threshold.

A 'lobbyist' must receive 'economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses,' so unpaid volunteer lobbyists are not lobbyists and thus are not subject to lobbyist licensing/registration requirements.
